text: This lesson closes out the chapter with a diagnostic checklist. The job didn't run, or the job ran but failed, are two of the most common tickets a DBA gets — and the answer is almost always in one of a small number of places.

sysjobhistory logs a row per step for every run Agent actually attempted, including the run status and a message column that usually contains the real error text — a CmdExec access-denied message is a strong hint the step is running under the wrong identity.

If a job never even attempted to start, sysjobhistory won't help at all. The next stop is SQL Server Agent's own error log, separate from the Database Engine's, viewable in SSMS — it logs the Agent service starting and stopping and schedule engine activity.

No history row at all points to the Agent service being stopped, a disabled schedule or job, or the job never being targeted at a server. A failed row that does exist usually points to a proxy or credential permission problem — checking history first tells you which bucket you're in.
